Motivation
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.
Changes
Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

Motivation
Enable candidate-only indexer scoring on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4.1, following
#40574
.
The current protocol already publishes compact candidate block IDs, but Hopper consumers still traverse the full logical score space before selecting among the candidates. This PR uses those block IDs during scoring, so consumers produce compact scores directly instead of a context-width score matrix.
The Triton implementation reads candidate K positions directly, avoiding a per-query
[queries, candidates, head_dim]
K tensor.

Prefill:
score candidate positions directly from shared BF16 index K with Triton. Per-request K retrieval/dequantization remains unchanged; no per-query candidate K tensor is materialized. Retain the independent Torch reference and fallback for unsupported shapes.

DeepSeek V4.1 on Hopper still uses:

What
Two fused paths for DeepSeek-V4.1, plus the MoE finalize plumbing they expose:
mHC sequence-parallel boundary
(
SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION
, opt-in): inside the sharded region each sublayer boundary becomes one collective launch — reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input — with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch (NVLS from three peers up, peer load/store at two ranks). With decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region ends at the tail boundary instead of excluding SP outright.
Engram
: the hash tables shard on hash-column boundaries in symmetric memory, and the lookup defaults to an in-place gather straight into
wkv
's MXFP8 operand — no all-reduce, no dequant/requant round trip (a bf16-dequantizing gather covers
wkv
configurations without an MXFP8 input path, exactly; the shared host table is read the same way). The gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine/norm fuse into one seam kernel with SP / DP / TP variants (
SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_TP_FUSION_MIN_TOKENS
gates the TP variant; the image-token mask rides the kernel as a per-row skip). CUDA only; ROCm and other platforms keep the existing paths.
MoE
: a raw
MoEOutput
's finalize now defers whenever the producer supports it and lands as one fused finalize + shared-add kernel writing the caller's buffer;
get_merged
honors
out=
on the unfused arm too, fixing a path where the sequence-parallel boundary read an unwritten buffer.
Accuracy
Kernel level: the direct gathers are bitwise-identical to the dequantizing reference (including e8m0 zero scales and fp8 denormal payloads) on both sm90 and sm100; the DP and SP seam variants are bitwise-identical to each other across row counts, ragged splits and skip masks, including NaN/Inf injection into masked rows; 200 back-to-back SP launches show stable semaphore rotation.
End to end (TP4/EP4, gsm8k 1319 questions, greedy): fused SP 0.9014 vs unfused 0.9113, McNemar p = 0.198 (not significant). A same-configuration rerun control scores 0.9113 / 0.9113 with only 36% exact-text agreement, i.e. the engine is not run-to-run stable at temperature 0 on this backend (as the cookbook documents), and the fused path's long-prompt logprob drift sits within that noise floor. TP-mode fusion scores 0.9052; TP2 (host table) 0.8954, all within the observed jitter band.
The seam consumes the previous boundary's lagged
pre
, so the fused math matches the unfused operator order; equivalence rather than bitwise identity is expected against the old path (the gate's sigmoid was already approximate there).
Notes
TP2 cannot hold the device tables beside the weights; the host table is the deployable form there (cookbook updated, along with the gather semantics).
Online weight updates remain rejected while derived hc weight splits are active; the probe follows the renamed stacked tensors.

#40417
Copy link
Description
Leoyzen
opened
on Sep 20, 2026
Issue body actions
Describe the bug
estimate_local_valid_shape_m()
in
python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
returns
topk_ids.nelement()
when no
expected_m
is given (~line 204, carries
# TODO: update for EP and DP
, introduced in
#23754
).
Under EP this counts the global routed elements.
local_expert_mapping
keeps the tensor shape unchanged and writes -1 for non-local experts, so
nelement()
= M_global x top_k, while each rank's GEMM only touches ~1/ep_size of those rows.
The value only drives kernel config selection: the Python block-size ladder in
_prepare_indexed_gemm_kwargs
and the humming launcher's variant lookup (
find_kernel_launch_data
in launcher.cpp). Correctness is unaffected, the launcher validates against real tensor shapes. So under EP every humming MoE GEMM picks its config for a workload ~4x larger than what the rank actually computes (EP4).
We tried the obvious fix, a graph-safe host estimate
max(1, M * top_k / ep_size)
(exact counting needs a D2H sync, illegal under CUDA graph capture). It moves every working point to the true local shape and passes unit tests, but serving regressed:
arm
decode tok/s/req
vs parent
parent (current code)
52.2
-
EP-aware estimate
49.5
-5.1% (perm p=0.003, n=10/arm)
EP-aware + ladder bands recalibrated from per-point kernel microbench
-
-4.0% e2e (C48 median, 3-arm check)
Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (384 routed experts, top_k 6, MXFP4 experts), TP4/EP4, 4x H200-class GPUs, DSPark speculative decoding, random workload at 32-48 concurrency, unique-seed A/B protocol with flush_cache between rounds, cross-session reproducible.
Per-cubin enumeration against the deployed heuristic ladder explains why. The ladder bands were calibrated against the global-element scale, and the two gemm types disagree about what the input even means:
indexed, routed rows ~750-2100: the local-rows input picks kernels 22-26% faster than the global-scale input
grouped, same points: opposite direction, the global-scale input wins by 8-12%
small decode CUDA-graph tiers (<200 rows): both land in the same band, zero effect
re-mapping ladder bands empirically flipped kernel rankings once real routing skew and CUDA-graph replay entered the picture
A single scalar cannot carry both total routed rows and per-expert density once num_local_experts != num_experts. For reference, the masked/DeepEP-LL path already uses
expected_m * num_local_experts
, and DeepEP-normal dispatch carries exact host-side
num_recv_tokens_per_expert
.
Reproduction
Any EP>1 run with
--moe-runner-backend humming
(default gemm type indexed). The wrong value is observable without serving, it is just
topk_ids.nelement()
under EP:
# decode bs=48, top_k=6, EP4: topk_ids (48, 6).nelement() = 288 passed as
# valid_shape_m while the rank's GEMM only handles ~72 rows.
# See estimate_local_valid_shape_m in
# python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
Serving A/B protocol:
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 384 --max-concurrency 48
, unique seed per round, /flush_cache between rounds, drop first warmup round, median of 4.
Environment
Python: 3.12.3, PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA: 13.0 (driver 580.105.08)
GPU 0-3: NVIDIA L20X (SM90)
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g20518d851, sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer: 0.6.18, triton: 3.7.1, transformers: 5.12.1
Possible fixes (for discussion)
(a) Document
valid_shape_m
as a hint defined on the global routed-element scale and leave the estimator as-is (what we reverted to; zero risk).
(b) Make ladder generation convention-aware per gemm_type and re-tune per device.
(c) Extend the launcher/config-selection API to take (rows, local expert count) or tokens-per-expert as a second key.
Happy to share the full A/B matrix and per-cubin timing data, attaching below.

Describe the bug
Serving

with
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK
on
2 nodes × 4 H200 (TP8 + EP8, LeaderWorkerSet, one 4-GPU pod per node over RoCE)
deterministically deadlocks during startup, right after the DSpark draft weights finish loading. Three consecutive attempts across two different images all hang at the same point with the same split stack; removing the DSPARK flags (identical everything else) starts cleanly in ~10 minutes.
The split we capture on every occurrence (py-spy dump, all 8 scheduler processes):
Node 0 schedulers (leader, TP0-3) — parked after
Load weight end ... type=DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark
:
monitored_barrier (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:5435)
dist_barrier_after_load (model_runner_components/load_model_utils.py:380)   # also seen :344 on dev-cu13
load_model (model_runner.py:1307)
initialize (model_runner.py:653)
Node 1 schedulers (worker, TP4-7) — parked earlier, inside the KV-pool memory probe:
all_reduce (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3252)
wrapper (torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py:83)
get_available_gpu_memory (utils/common.py:550)
_profile_available_bytes (kv_cache_configurator.py:2214)
The worker-side ranks have posted the memory-probe all-reduce and wait for the leader-side ranks, while the leader-side ranks wait at a different synchronization point (post-load barrier). The two node halves sit at mismatched collective sites permanently — GPU utilization 0%, GPU memory and logs frozen from that point on. No watchdog fires (the stall happens before the scheduler loop starts).
This looks like the same unsynchronized-decision family as
#39886
(DSpark CUDA-graph memory check not synchronized across ranks → ranks disagree on collective participation) and the runtime variant in
#33289
(multi-node TP + DSpark → per-rank divergence → unmatched collectives). Our case adds a multi-node TP8/EP8 startup reproduction with full per-node py-spy stacks.

Issue body actions
We are evaluating an MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 GEMM on NVIDIA H100.
The fused-E8M0 Humming kernel is numerically correct, but with group-32
MXFP8 activation scales it is significantly slower than both:
Humming's generic group-scale path
A QDQ baseline that dequantizes both operands and then runs a BF16 GEMM
We would like to ask whether group-32 MXFP8 input scaling is an intended
performance target and whether there are plans to optimize this case on Hopper.
Quantization format
The operands use the following format:
Activation payload: FP8 E4M3
Activation scale: per-token, per-K-group power-of-two scale
Activation group size: 32
Weight payload: MXFP4 E2M1
Weight scale: E8M0

Summary
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch using three shared-memory TMA buffers per dispatch warp.
Previously, a dispatch warp prepared tokens sequentially around remote S2G stores. With this change, the next token's hidden data, scale factors, metadata, and routing information are prefetched while previous remote stores remain in flight.
At steady state, the three buffers are used for:
A previous token whose remote S2G store may still be in flight.
The current token being sent to remote ranks.
The next token being prefetched from global memory.
Before recycling the oldest buffer,
tma_store_wait<1>()
reduces the number of outstanding store groups to one. This keeps buffer reuse safe without fully draining all remote stores between tokens.
The shared-memory calculation now accounts for all three staging buffers, and direct NVLink dispatch is limited to at most 14 dispatch warps. The non-NVLink path remains single-buffered.

The multi-buffer TMA scheduling and matching shared-memory sizing appear consistent across NVLink and non-NVLink paths, with outstanding stores flushed before buffer reuse.
v4
The dispatch kernel switches from single per-warp staging (drained fully per token) to three round-robin staging TMA buffers per dispatch warp. While the current token's remote S2G/NVLink/RDMA store stays in flight, the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing is prefetched into the buffer whose previous use is the oldest outstanding store group (deterministically token_iter - 2 of 3, or none on a warm-up iteration); tma_store_wait<1>() retires that group before the buffer is overwritten, and the final barrier drains the last in-flight store. The host sizes per-warp smem by 3x (RDMA: 1x) and caps NVLink dispatch warps at 14, with the RDMA path remaining single-buffered and full-drained (unchanged behavior). Edge cases (first iteration, last token skipped, warps with no tokens, per-token global slot/counter writes) are all safe and unchanged. Measured on 8xH100 dispatch goes 250->280 GB/s, combine unchanged. Overall the change correctly and faithfully implements the PR as a pure pipelining/perf optimization on the previously single-buffered path.
v3
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch by switching from double- to triple-buffered TMA staging (kNumDirectNVLinkTmaBuffers 2->3, kNumTmaBuffers 2->3 for the NVLink path), and refactoring the per-token body into a
prepare_token
lambda so the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing can be prefetched while the current token's remote S2G stores are in flight. The phase tracking was generalized from two scalars (phase_0/phase_1) to a
phases[kNumTmaBuffers]
array, and buffer indexing changed from bitmask (
& (kNumTmaBuffers-1)
) to modulo (
% kNumTmaBuffers
) to support 3 (non-power-of-two) buffers. The host-side shared-memory computation already multiplies by num_tma_buffers and caps direct NVLink dispatch at 14 warps.
Correctness analysis (all verified sound):
Buffer-reuse safety: In steady state, entering iteration N up to 2 store groups (iters N-2, N-1) are outstanding.
tma_store_wait<1>()
retires iter N-2's store (which read buffer (N-2)%3 == (N+1)%3) before prepare_token(N+1) writes into that same buffer. This correctly matches the recycled buffer to the just-retired store group, so triple buffering is safe.
Per-buffer mbarrier phases persist across reuse (buffer b used at iters b, b+3, ...), and
phases[]
is zero-initialized; flip semantics are preserved.
The buffer indexing change to
% kNumTmaBuffers
is applied consistently in both prepare_token and the main loop and is required because 3 is not a power of two.
The NVLink prefetch (prepare_token for the next token) is issued before awaiting the current buffer's load arrival, correctly overlapping the next token's G2S load with the current token's remote S2G store; it targets a distinct buffer with an independent mbarrier so there is no cross-buffer hazard.
Non-NVLink path stays single-buffered (kNumTmaBuffers=1) and keeps a full
tma_store_wait()

next_token_idx < num_tokens
guards.

Purpose
With
--moe-backend humming
and expert parallelism, Humming runs DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 experts on its grouped GEMM. On Hopper the indexed GEMM is much faster for this model. This PR makes
get_humming_moe_gemm_type()
return
indexed
when all of these hold:
the experts are MXFP4 with DeepSeek V4 routing;
model_type
is
deepseek_v41
or
deepseek_v41_text
;
the device is CUDA SM90;
there are no all2all kernels, or the backend is
allgather_reducescatter
.
Without EP, Humming already picks indexed, so nothing changes there.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
still overrides the choice. Since
#56997
, Humming is the default MXFP4 MoE backend on SM90, so V4.1 with EP on Hopper otherwise runs the grouped GEMM by default; this PR moves that default path to indexed too. The rule applies with BF16 activations and with per-token FP8 activations (
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
).
The MXFP4 MoE method (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3, plain mxfp4) now runs
quantization_config.moe.activation
:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
Humming takes the named format as a fixed input schema, with its input-schema fallback off.
Other explicit backends must run the named format, and
auto
keeps only the backends that do. Before, these models ignored the name on every backend. Now a backend that does not run it stops vLLM, on every platform (CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU). The DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE backends (
deep_gemm_mega_moe
,
aiter_mega_moe
) build their own experts and do not read the name. On ROCm, the Kimi-K3 AITER path, which skips the backend selector, now refuses a named activation instead of ignoring it. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
now stops vLLM instead of running MXFP8. A draft model with its own
speculative_config.moe_backend
inherits the target's
quantization_config
, so the same rule applies to it.
The startup log prints the format Humming runs:
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. The line appears for every Humming MoE model, gpt-oss included.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load. Humming has no e8m0 input scales on WGMMA, and humming 0.1.16 rejects fp32 group scales with MXFP4 weights (
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
). Group-wise scales are also 1.2x to 24x slower than per-token in the SM90 Humming GEMM at M >= 256 (numbers in the review reply).
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
still works as on main, with no early check: a format Humming cannot run fails while the weights convert, as before. With
--moe-backend humming
, setting it together with
moe.activation
is an error.
gpt-oss is unchanged. With no name, nothing changes.

I would either make the per-token FP8 path opt-in for now, or evaluate this more exhaustively before making it default, e.g. on agentic evals.

# every (tile_n, n_thr) pair is one more kernel to compile. Tuned on GB300
# (hc_mult 4, hidden_size 5120 and 7168) against the separate post + split-k
# GEMM it replaces; the bands are coarse because the loss against a per-shape
# optimum is ~1-2%, while one fixed config gives up to 18% at the top of the
# range.
_FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR = 128
_FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS = 32


def mhc_fused_post_pre_split_config(
    num_tokens: int, hidden_size: int, hc_mult: int
) -> tuple[int, int, int] | None:
    """Pick ``(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr)`` for the fused post + pre-norm GEMM.

    Returns None when a separate post kernel followed by a split-k GEMM is the
    better choice, or when the hidden size does not divide evenly across the
    fused kernel's block. One source of truth for the dispatch decision, the
    compile key and the launch, which must agree.
    """
    if num_tokens > _FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS:
        return None
    n_thr = _FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR
    if hidden_size % n_thr:
        return None
    # The projection tiles supply the parallelism a small token count cannot,
    # so the tile grows with the batch: 1.3x at one token and 1.03x at 32
    # against a split-k GEMM given the split its own estimator computes.
    if num_tokens < 16:
        tile_n, n_splits = 2, 8
    else:
        tile_n, n_splits = 6, 8
    # The kernel drops projection tiles and k-slices it cannot fill evenly.
    mix_size = hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)
    while tile_n > 1 and mix_size % tile_n:
        tile_n -= 1
    while n_splits > 1 and hidden_size % (n_splits * n_thr):
        n_splits //= 2
    return tile_n, n_splits, n_thr

def supports_mhc_overlap(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    """Check kernel requirements and safety of sharing the coefficient stream."""
    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
    # DeepGEMM's prenorm kernel requires K % 64 == 0, N % 8 == 0, and N <= 32.
    mix_size = config.hc_mult * (config.hc_mult + 2)
    return (

        and config.hidden_size % 64 == 0

def supports_mhc_all_reduce(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    parallel = vllm_config.parallel_config
